builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Beyond Hard Tokens: Predictive Memory for Multimodal Protein Generation
summary: PredMem replaces the stateless mask reset in iterative masked decoding of multimodal protein language models, carrying a probability-weighted Top-k expectation embedding of uncommitted predictions forward as a soft anchor instead of resetting unresolved sites to an identical [MASK] embedding. It costs nothing in extra denoiser forward passes or training; the only overhead is summarizing logits and an affine interpolation into masked inputs, plus new hyperparameters (k and the interpolation weight) to tune. It can fail if the stabilized early trajectories entrench poor initial beliefs, if the reader's workloads are anchored/conditional rather than open-ended co-generation where gains are claimed, or if it is applied outside the masked discrete diffusion decoding setting where the mechanism does not transfer.
rationale: The method is training-free and adds no denoiser compute, so it is cheap to validate, but the gains are specific to multimodal masked protein generation and must be confirmed on the reader's actual models and workloads.
technique: Predictive Memory self-conditioning for masked protein decoding

claims.statement: PredMem replaces the stateless mask reset in iterative masked decoding of multimodal protein language models, carrying a probability-weighted Top-k expectation embedding of uncommitted predictions forward as a soft anchor instead of resetting unresolved sites to an identical [MASK] embedding. It costs nothing in extra denoiser forward passes or training; the only overhead is summarizing logits and an affine interpolation into masked inputs, plus new hyperparameters (k and the interpolation weight) to tune. It can fail if the stabilized early trajectories entrench poor initial beliefs, if the reader's workloads are anchored/conditional rather than open-ended co-generation where gains are claimed, or if it is applied outside the masked discrete diffusion decoding setting where the mechanism does not transfer.

Raises unconditional sequence-structure co-generation success by 3.6, 17.7, and 48.7 percentage points on DPLM-2, DPLM-2.1, and ESM3 respectively, with improved quality-diversity trade-off and reduced repetitive mode collapse.
